items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I have a young fellow by the name of Jeb Patton who is going to be in that same vein... I’ve been training people to do just that.

ctx.x: Yeah that would be it. You know one of my mentors was Art Tatum. And he was truly a concert pianist. Whenever he played, no matter what he played, it was like a concert piece. And Horowitz — the violinist, I can’t think — anyway three famous concert musicians went into hear him play one night and they came away saying if this man had wanted to be a classical pianist he probably would have been the greatest classical pianist who ever lived. Because he would make up all that music on the spot. And still, this is…
Were you sent overseas for the Korean War?
